items.title: 코스피, 나스닥 반등에도 '팔자'폭 확대…SK하이닉스 4% 약세

items.title: 공사채 5년물 유찰 속속…크레디트 약세 속 'AAA' 수급 경계감
items.snippet: 국고채 금리가 큰 폭으로 하락하면서 레벨을 낮췄으나 크레디트물의 약세는 쉽사리 꺾이지 않고 있다.얇아진 투자심리 속에서 'AAA' 공기업들은 5년물 채권 입찰 후 유찰을 택하는 사례도 늘고 있다.외국인 매수세가 국고채 강세를 이끌면서 절대금리 레벨이 낮아진 점은 공기업의 조달 비용 부담을 소폭 낮췄으나 여전히 크레디트 시장 투자 심리는 회복되지 않는 모습이다.국내 기관 투자자들은 짙은 관망세를 이어가면서 'AAA' 공사채와 은행채 수급 여건 등을 살피고 있다.◇크레디트 약세 속 5년물 공사채 조달 흔들20일 투자은행(IB) 업계

items.title: LG생활건강, 높아진 눈높이에 3분기 '주춤'…에이본 매각 부담도

items.title: 폭염에도 고마진 상품 '쑥쑥'…BGF리테일, 3Q 영업익 6% 증가 전망

items.title: 반도체 공정서도 나오는 '영원한 화학물질'…폐수 관리 사각지대
items.snippet: 반도체 제조공정에서 사용되거나 발생할 수 있는 과불화화합물(PFAS)이 새로운 환경관리 과제로 떠오르고 있다.반도체 생산시설이 대규모로 확대되고 있지만, 국내에는 산업폐수에 포함된 PFAS에 대한 별도의 배출허용기준이 마련돼 있지 않아서다.PFAS는 자연환경에서 쉽게 분해되지 않아 '영원한 화학물질'로 불린다. 일부 물질은 인체와 생태계에 유해한 영향을 미치는 것으로 알려져 있다.반도체뿐 아니라 화학·섬유·도금 등 다양한 산업에서 사용되는 만큼 배출원을 파악하고 관리체계를 마련해야 한다는 지적이 나온다.◇ 반도체 공정서도 발생하는

items.title: AI 대형주 독주 쉬어가나…DB證 "내년 코스닥 종목장세"

items.title: 李 “전작권 반드시 조기 환수”… 북핵엔 “최후 방어 무기”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 19일 전시작전통제권 전환에 대해 “주권 국가로서의 최소한의 요건”이라며 “반드시 조기에 환수해야 된다”고 밝혔다. 한미 정보협력 균열 우려에 대해선 “국익을 지켜나가는 과정에서 생기는 작은 이견”이라고 말했다. 이 대통령은 취임 500일(16일)을 맞아 이날 청와대 춘추관을 예고 없이 방문해 90분간 출입기자단과 오찬 및 차담회를 갖고 “국가 방위 권한을 다른 나라에 맡기고 전쟁 때는 그들의 지휘에 따르는데 혹시 지휘를 안 하면 어떻게 할 것이냐”며 “국가 간 관계에서 그런 일이 없으리라는 보장이 없다”고 말했다. 이어 “한미 간 기본적으로는 돌려받는 쪽으로 잘 협의되고 있다”고 했다. 제이비어 브런슨 주한미군사령관이 북핵·미사일 고도화 등을 들어 ‘상황이 달라졌다’는 취지로 말한 데 대해선 “충분히 스스로 감당할 수 있다는...

items.title: 北 김여정 또 적반하장 “대남 확성기 재개 검토”
items.snippet: 김여정 북한 노동당 총무부장이 19일 “대한국 확성기 방송을 재개하는 문제를 검토하고 있다”고 말했다. 비무장지대(DMZ) 지뢰 폭발 사건에도 정부가 대북 확성기 방송 재개에 거리를 둔 가운데, 북한군의 군사분계선(MDL) 침범에 대한 우리 군의 경고 사격에 적반하장식 공세에 나선 것이다. 김정은 북한 국무위원장의 여동생인 김여정은 이날 담화에서 “지금 남부 국경의 상황은 매우 불안정하다”며 “(한국군이) 우리 인원들이 ‘월선’하였다고 근거 없는 트집을 걸면서 자동보총과 대구경기관총으로 경고사격을 가하고 있다”고 주장했다. 이어 “무모한 객기는 분명 엄청난 정세 위기를 확대시키며 커다란 재앙을 스스로 불러오게 될 것”이라며 “우리 군사 지도부는 전술적 타격 수단들을 전 남부 국경선 부근에 증강 배치하는 문제와 대한국 확성기 방송을 재개하는 문...

items.title: 秋 징계 미룬 與… “재정 쭉쭉 빨아먹어” 옹호로 또 민심 불질러

items.title: 소방관 조문 김민석 차량, ‘응급환자 구역’ 주차 논란
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 김민석 대표가 탑승한 차량이 18일 순직 소방관 조문 당시 응급환자 전용 주차구역에 주차한 사실이 알려지며 논란이 일었다. 민주당은 “운전자가 해당 주차 공간이 응급환자 전용 구간임을 인지하지 못했다”고 사과했다. 당 대표 비서실장인 김태선 의원은 19일 페이스북에 “순직 소방관 조문 당시 응급환자 전용 주차구역에 주차된 차량은 저희 의원실 차량”이라며 “국민 여러분께 심려를 끼쳐드린 점 진심으로 사과드리며 다시는 이런 일이 없도록 각별히 주의하겠다”고 밝혔다. 김 대표는 전날 오후 8시 50분경 경기 부천시 순천향대 부천병원 장례식장에 마련된 고 김진석 소방위의 빈소를 찾아 조문했는데, 당시 김 대표를 병원 입구에 내려준 차량은 응급환자 전용 구역에 주차했다. 민주당 신현영 대변인은 “해당 차량은 병원에 도착해 당 대표와 비서실...

items.snippet: “스스로 작전할 수 있는지 확인하고 넘겨주겠다는 게 고맙긴 한데 우리 스스로 해야 할 일이 아닌가 생각한다.” 이재명 대통령은 19일 기자간담회에서 전시작전통제권(전작권)의 신속한 전환을 강조하며 이같이 말했다. 정부의 전작권 조기 전환 추진에 미국이 ‘조건’ 충족을 강조하며 한미 간 이견이 본격화된 가운데 군사주권과 자주국방 차원에서 조기 전환의 당위성을 강조한 것. 전작권 전환 시 고도화된 북핵·미사일 위협에 대응이 약화될 수 있다는 우려에 대해선 “(북핵은) 최후 방어 무기에 해당한다”고 말했다. 일각에선 북핵을 ‘체제 방어용’으로 규정하면서 핵 불균형에 대한 대응 필요성을 평가절하한 것 아니냐는 지적이 나온다.● “북핵은 최후 방어 무기” 이 대통령은 이날 전작권 관련 질의에 “대한민국은 자주적인 독립국가”라며 “국가로서의 최소한의 요...

items.title: 李 “지배경영권 남용 등에 증시 저평가” 기업에 화살
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 최근 이어진 국내 증시 하락세에 대해 “(주가가) 많이 오르면 조정이 불가피하다”면서도 “다만 대한민국 주식시장은 매우 저평가된 게 사실”이라고 말했다. 그 이유로 기업 지배경영권 남용을 언급하며 추가 대책을 예고했다. 이 대통령은 19일 청와대 춘추관에서 기자단과 만나 최근 코스피 하락으로 국민연금이 보유한 국내 주식 평가액이 크게 줄었다는 질문을 받고 “주식시장이 부동산시장이랑 비슷하지만 어느 일방향으로 끝까지 갈 수 없다”며 이같이 말했다. “과거와 다르게 정부가 금융시장, 증권시장에 직접 개입하기 어렵고, 바람직하지도 않다”고도 했다. 국내 주식시장이 저평가된 이유로 이 대통령은 “지배경영구조, 시장의 투명성, 대한민국의 지정학적 위상, 산업경제 정책의 불확실성” 등을 꼽았다. 그러면서 “이 중 정책 불확실성은 많이 개...

items.title: 李 “SNS 없었으면 나도 없다… 목숨줄-숨구멍”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 19일 소셜네트워크서비스(SNS) 게시글이 크게 늘어난 데 대해 “SNS가 없었으면 이재명 대통령이 있었을까. 과연 경기도지사가 되고 그 후에 집중된 포화 속에서 살아남을 수 있었을까”라고 말했다. 국무회의 생중계를 줄여야 한다는 지적에 대해선 “하급 공무원도 아닌 일국의 장관인데 그걸 누가 지켜보고 있기 때문에 반박할 수 없다는 건 바람직하지 않다”고 일축했다. 이 대통령은 이날 “(SNS는) 저의 장점이라고 생각한다”며 “제가 목숨줄이라고 표현했다”고 말했다. 이어 “정치하는 분들에게도 국민과의 직접 소통을 늘려라, SNS를 많이 하라고 한다”며 “어느 순간에 본인을 살릴 숨구멍은 SNS”라고 강조했다. ‘목숨줄’과 ‘숨구멍’에 비유하며 SNS 활동을 이어가겠다는 뜻을 분명히 한 것이다. 이 대통령은 일부 SNS 게시글이...

items.snippet: 이찬진 금융감독원장이 단일종목 레버리지 상장지수펀드(ETF)의 상장 일정을 맞추기 위해 심사를 빨리 진행한 측면이 있다고 밝혔다. 금융 당국이 고위험 상품인 단일종목 레버리지 상품의 상장 여부를 졸속으로 심사하는 바람에 2조 원이 넘는 투자 손실을 초래했다는 비판을 피하기 어려울 것으로 보인다. 19일 국회 정무위원회 금감원 국감에서 이 원장은 “4월 중순 금융위원회에서 (단일종목 레버리지) 상장 일정을 정책적으로 발표한 게 있다”면서 “그 일정을 맞추기 위해 심사를 빨리 한 부분이 있다”고 말했다. 단일종목 레버리지 상품은 올해 5월 27일 16개 종목이 상장됐다.● 단일종목 레버리지, 일반 ETF의 절반 만에 이뤄져 국민의힘 박대출 의원은 통상 ETF 종목 상장 시 한국거래소 예비 심사와 금감원 증권신고서 심사 등 2단계를 거치는데, 단일...

items.snippet: 검찰청이 폐지되면서 출범한 공소청에 대한 첫 국정감사에서는 이재명 대통령 관련 사건의 공소취소 가능성이 쟁점이 됐다. 이 대통령 사건의 공소유지를 맡은 서울중앙·수원지방공소청은 공소취소를 검토하거나 법무부와 협의한 적 없다고 밝혔다. 19일 국회 법제사법위원회 국정감사에서 박철우 서울중앙지방공소청장은 이 대통령 사건에 대한 공소취소 가능성을 묻는 질의에 “국민적 관심이 매우 높다는 건 알지만 여느 사건과 다를 바 없다”며 “개별 사건에 대해 어떻게 하겠다고 말씀드릴 수 없는 게 원칙”이라고 말했다. 김봉현 수원지방공소청장도 쌍방울 대북송금 사건을 두고 ‘(법무부 검찰인권존중미래위원회) 진상조사단에서 공소취소를 요청하면 응하겠느냐’는 질의에 “요청받은 적 없다”며 “사건이 재판 중에 있다”고 했다. 서울중앙지방공소청은 이 대통령의 대장동·백현동...

items.snippet: 국립중앙박물관(국중박)에서 개최한 전시에 출품한 유물이 개인 소유라는 걸 숨겼다가 ‘셀프 검증·전시’ 비판을 받고 있는 유홍준 중앙박물관장이 19일 국정감사장에서 “중대한 착오이자 불찰”이라며 고개를 숙였다. 하지만 야당 의원들은 “명백한 규정 위반”이라며 사퇴를 촉구했다. 국중박은 7∼10월 개최한 특별전 ‘우리들의 밥상’에 전시한 ‘일반시국은(一飯是國恩)’이 일제강점기 고위 관료 박중양(1874∼1959)의 글씨로 드러나 8월 철거했다. 그런데 이 유묵이 최근 국감을 앞두고 유 관장이 2019년 경매를 통해 5만 원에 구입한 개인 소장품임이 드러났다. 유 관장은 이날 국회 문화체육관광위원회 국감에서 “작품을 전시에 내놓으며 소장품이라 밝히지 않은 건 저 개인의 자랑이 될까 봐 안 했던 것”이라고 해명했다. 앞서 검증 결과를 발표할 때도 소...

items.title: 같은 국가직인데… 경찰청은 국가 예산, 소방청은 지자체 예산
items.snippet: 소방관은 국가직 공무원이지만 월급과 장비 구입비는 대부분 지방자치단체가 부담한다. 올해 전국 소방 예산 8조5949억원 중 지자체 몫은 7조6151억원(88.6%)이다. 국가가 지원하는 예산은 10% 정도다. 내년에는 지원금이 약 2900억원(27.6%) 줄어든다. 2020년 지역 간 소방 인력의 격차를 줄이겠다며 소방공무원을 지방직에서 국가직으로 전환했지만 예산 구조는 그대로인 것이다. 지자체에서는 “국가직으로 바뀐 지 6년이 지났는데 부담은 여태껏 지자체가 지고 있다”는 불만이 나온다. 전문가들은 “국가와 지자체의 소방 예산 분담 구조를 다시 짜야 한다”고 지적한다.

items.title: 송파 경찰병원 의사 부족한데, 1253억 들여 아산에 또 추진
items.snippet: 서울 송파구에 있는 경찰병원은 경찰 공무원 진료를 전담하는 경찰청장 소속 국립병원이다. 그런데 경찰병원이 전문의·전공의 등 의료진을 제대로 채우지 못해 진료 시간까지 줄이고 있다. 이런 상황에서 경찰은 의사 58명이 필요한 제2경찰병원 건립을 추진하고 있다. 경찰청이 국민의힘 서명옥 의원실에 제출한 자료를 보면, 지난 8월 기준 경찰병원 정원 678명 가운데 52명이 공석이었다. 의사는 22명이 정원에 모자랐다. 전문의가 정원 75명 중 9명, 전공의는 정원 48명 중 13명이 공석이었다. 2021년부터 올해까지 의원면직으로 경찰병원을 떠난 전문의는 28명. 이에 따라 경찰병원 진료 시간도 총 23세션, 69시간이 줄었다. 진료 환자 수도 2023년 32만8090명에서 2025년 27만5434명으로 줄었다.

items.title: 가평엔 벌써 노란 카펫 깔렸네
items.snippet: 19일 오후 경기 가평군 북면의 한 카페 뒤뜰. 전날 내린 가을비에 은행잎이 우수수 떨어졌다. 어느새 노란 카펫이 깔렸다. 비가 그친 뒤 공기도 한결 선선해졌다. 한 시민이 가을 풍경을 감상하고 있다. 기상청은 21일 또 비가 내린 뒤 기온이 더 떨어질 것이라고 예상했다.

items.title: 전자발찌 채우면 뭐하나… 범죄자 870명 늘때 관리자는 20명 줄어
items.snippet: 지난 13일 인천 남동구 구월동에서 흉기 난동을 벌인 최충락(59)은 전자발찌를 차고 있었다. 전자발찌는 재범 위험이 큰 범죄자 위치를 실시간으로 파악하는 장치다. 재범을 막기 위해서다. 하지만 전자발찌는 살인 미수 전과가 있는 최충락의 범행을 막지 못했다. 19일 경기 성남에서는 경찰에 신변 보호를 요청해 스마트워치를 지급받은 60대 여성이 전 남편이 휘두른 흉기에 찔려 다치는 사건이 발생했다. 스마트워치는 성폭력·가정폭력 피해자 등 신변 보호가 필요한 사람에게 지급된다. 버튼을 누르면 곧바로 경찰에 도움을 요청할 수 있는 기기다. 이처럼 범죄 가해자를 관리하고 피해자를 보호하기 위한 장치를 도입했지만 강력 범죄를 막지 못하는 일이 잇따르고 있다.

items.title: 광수단, 유력인사 수사 지지부진… 김승원·한동훈 의혹까지 맡을 듯
items.snippet: 서울경찰청은 19일 김승원(더불어민주당) 의원과 한동훈(무소속) 의원 관련 의혹 사건을 서울청 광역수사단에 배당할 예정이라고 밝혔다. 유시민씨 관련 명예훼손 고발 사건도 광수단이 맡았다. 검찰 폐지 후 경찰이 굵직한 사건을 떠맡으면서 서울청 광수단이 바빠지고 있다. 서울청 광수단이 맡을 김승원 의원 사건은 김 의원이 코로나 치료제 개발 업체 제넨셀 청탁을 받고 식품의약품안전처에 임상 시험 관련 민원을 전달했다는 의혹이다. 한동훈 의원 사건은 김승원 의원이 법무부 장관 후보자에 지명되자 한 의원이 제넨셀 청탁 관련 의혹을 제기하면서 검찰 내부 수사 자료를 공개했다는 의혹 사건이다.

items.title: 도쿄보다 많은 서울 공중화장실… 정작 외국인은 “못 찾겠어요”
items.snippet: 인도네시아에서 온 관광객 애슐리(19)양은 지난 18일 서울 마포구 망원시장을 구경하다가 화장실을 찾느라 애를 먹었다. 구글맵에 ‘restroom(화장실)’을 검색했지만 반경 50m 안에는 한 곳도 표시되지 않았다. 화장실을 찾아 15분을 헤맸다는 애슐리양은 “구글맵에 나온 공중화장실도 건물 안에 있어 입구를 찾기 어려웠다”고 했다.

items.snippet: 최근 건축계에서 가장 화제인 작품 중 하나가 지난달 개관한 미국 로스앤젤레스의 ‘루카스 내러티브 아트 뮤지엄’입니다. ‘스타워즈’로 유명한 영화감독 조지 루카스와 그의 아내 멜로디 홉슨이 사재 10억달러(약 1조3400억원)를 털어 만들었어요. 독특한 외관이 특징인데요. 곡선으로 휘어지고 솟은 건물은 지상에 착륙한 우주선처럼 보여요. 거대한 건물 한가운데를 아치처럼 들어 올려 그 아래에 광장을 만들었어요. 광장 위로는 4개 층을 관통하는 타원형 천창을 통해 하늘을 올려다볼 수 있죠.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [사소한 역사] 한 번 걸리면 50일까지 앓았던 ‘고뿔’ 세종대왕이 감기 꾀병 부린 까닭은?
items.snippet: 올해는 독감 유행이 일찍 시작됐어요. 질병관리청은 지난달 11일 전국에 독감 유행 주의보를 발령했습니다. 현대에는 독감이나 감기에 걸리면 해열제를 비롯해 다양한 약을 써요. 하지만 이런 약이 없던 과거에는 감기에 걸리는 걸 더욱 걱정했습니다. 과거 우리나라에서 감기를 부르는 말은 고뿔이었어요. ‘코에 불이 난다’는 의미인데요. 감기에 걸려 기침을 하고 콧물을 쏟아내면 코가 아프기 때문에 그런 명칭이 붙은 것으로 보입니다. 현대에는 일반 감기와 인플루엔자 바이러스가 일으키는 독감을 서로 구분하지만, 둘을 명확히 나눌 수 없었던 과거에는 감기 자체에 걸리는 것을 경계했죠.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [노벨 물리학상] 지구 관통하는 ‘우주의 유령’… 남극 얼음에서 잡아냈죠
items.snippet: 영화에 나오는 유령처럼 어떤 물질이라도 그냥 통과하는 존재가 있습니다. 바로 우주 만물을 이루는 기본 입자 중 하나인 중성미자입니다. 다른 물질과 거의 반응하지 않고 지나가 ‘우주의 유령’이라고 부릅니다. 올해 노벨 물리학상은 남극 얼음 속 천문대인 아이스큐브(IceCube)에서 우주의 유령을 추적해 온 프랜시스 할젠(82) 미국 위스콘신대 매디슨 교수에게 돌아갔습니다. 중성미자는 우주가 탄생한 빅뱅 직후에도 나왔고, 태양의 핵융합이나 원전(原電)의 핵분열 반응에서도 나옵니다. 질량이 거의 없고 전하(정전기의 양)도 띠지 않아 다른 물질과 반응을 하지 않지만, 우주에서 빛의 최소 단위인 광자 다음으로 흔한 입자입니다. 지금 이 순간에도 태양에서 날아온 중성미자 650억개가 새끼손톱 하나 크기의 면적(약 1㎠)을 매초 지나가고 있습니다.

items.snippet: 지난 16일 경기 부천의 금속 공장 화재 현장에서 진화 작업을 하다 중태에 빠진 김진석(44) 소방위가 다음 날 새벽 숨졌다. 김 소방위는 퇴근을 20여 분 앞두고 현장에 가장 먼저 출동했다. 내년 초등학교 입학을 앞둔 여섯 살 딸을 둔 가장이었다. 순천향대 부천병원 장례식장에 마련된 빈소에는 시민과 동료 소방관들의 추모 발길이 이어졌다. 이재명 대통령은 17일 빈소를 찾아 유족을 위로했다. 정부는 김 소방위를 소방장에서 소방위로 1계급 특진시키고 옥조근정훈장을 추서했다.

items.title: 철도 깔고, 도로 다듬고… 기업과 사람이 모이는 ‘활력 도시’로
items.snippet: 지역 곳곳을 연결하는 철도와 도로망이 확충되면서 기업하기 좋은 여건이 만들어졌다. 그러자 양질의 일자리를 찾아 사람들이 몰려왔다. 대구 달성군 이야기다. 2016년 22만3585명이던 달성군 인구는 올해 6월 말 기준 26만339명으로 16%이상 늘었다. 1995년 3월 대구시 편입 당시보다는 두 배 이상으로 증가했다. 4곳이던 산업단지는 8곳으로 늘어났다. 지난 6월 지방선거를 통해 재선에 성공한 최재훈 달성군수는 초선 때부터 시민들이 오가는 대중교통 확장은 물론 기업들의 물류 여건 개선 등 교통 인프라 확충에 공을 들였다. 결국 대형 국책 사업 유치도 연이어 성공했다. 편리한 교통과 일자리 덕분에 주민도 늘고, 이들의 삶도 빛나는 선순환이 이어지고 있는 것이다.

items.title: Molecular Doping of MoS$_2$ with N-Heterocyclic Carbenes: A Raman Study of Interfacial Charge Transfer
items.abstract: We demonstrate efficient electron doping of exfoliated MoS$_2$ through the deposition of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) molecules onto its surface. Raman spectroscopy reveals a pronounced softening of the optical A$_{1g}$ phonon mode after NHC deposition, consistent with electron transfer from the NHC molecules to the MoS$_2$ layers. The largest phonon-energy shifts are observed in monolayer and bilayer flakes whereas changes in bulk-like MoS$_2$ are negligible, indicating that the doping efficiency depends on the number of layers. This thickness dependence highlights the dominant role of interfacial charge transfer at the NHC/MoS$_2$ interface. Quantitative analysis of the Raman modes of as-exfoliated and NHC-covered MoS$_2$, together with comparison with literature values, allows us to estimate an increase in the two-dimensional electron density of about two-orders of magnitude in MoS$_2...

items.title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As$_2$) to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. items.abstract: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. items.title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
items.abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and tran...

items.title: Gate-defined quantum dot and charge noise analysis in a Forksheet transistor
items.abstract: We report the cryogenic characterization of a 14-nm nMOS Forksheet transistor down to 10 mK. We demonstrate that the device retains transistor operation with improved characteristics at cryogenic temperatures, while also forming a gate-defined quantum dot that can be tuned to the single-electron regime. In the quantum-dot regime, we perform low-frequency charge-noise measurements across different charge occupations and observe an average charge-noise amplitude of $\langle S_0\rangle = 10\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ at 1 Hz, with a minimum measured value of $3.3\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results highlight the potential of Forksheet technology for the monolithic cointegration of quantum and classical CMOS functionalities in future quantum processors.

items.title: Revealing Detailed Transport Mechanisms in Silicon Tunneling Diodes
items.abstract: Understanding carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions is essential for developing next-generation tunneling devices for cryogenic electronics and steep-slope technologies. In this work, we investigate the transport mechanisms in a silicon tunneling diode using extensive TCAD (Technology Computer Aided Design) simulations benchmarked against electrical measurements over a wide temperature range of 4 K to 440 K. The measured device characteristics show no negative differential conductance, strong temperature dependence of forward current with a nearly constant semi-logarithmic slope, and weak temperature dependence under high reverse bias. To identify the mechanisms underlying these characteristics, we investigate the contributions of band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), trap-assisted tunneling (TAT), Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination, and avalanche generation. items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.abstract: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. items.snippet: 스카치위스키가 위기라고 한다. 스코틀랜드 창고에서 숙성 중인 오크통은 약 2200만 통, 50억L가 넘는다. 영국 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 이 가운데 팔릴 양보다 더 만들어 쌓아 둔 잉여 원액만 14억L에 달한다고 보도했다. 10년 전 4억L에도 못 미치던 양이 3.5배 이상으로 불어난 것이다. 2008년 리먼 브러더스 사태 이후 저금리로 갈 곳 잃은 돈이 위스키 같은 실물자산으로 몰렸다. 결정적 계기는 코로나19였다. ‘홈술’ 열풍 속에 오래 두고 마실 수 있는 위스키가 주목받았다. 업계가 더 많이 만들어 쌓아 둔 건 당연한 선택이었다.

items.title: 우리의 밤은 당신의 낮보다 아름답다
items.snippet: 파리 몽마르트르의 밤을 누군가의 이름으로 기억한다면 단연 앙리 드 툴루즈 로트레크(1864~1901)일 것이다. 화려한 무대, 객석의 웃음소리, 술잔 위로 내려앉은 짙은 피로까지 그가 캔버스에 담아낸 장면들은 지금도 당대의 환희를 생생히 되살린다. 전설적인 카바레 ‘물랭 루주’가 오늘날에도 그의 이름을 딴 툴루즈 로트레크 메뉴를 선보이며 경의를 표하는 까닭이며 세상이 그에게 ‘몽마르트르의 혼’이라는 찬사를 바치는 이유다. 부유한 귀족 출신 화가는 어쩌다 무희와 가수, 거리의 여성들이 살아가는 밤의 환락가를 그리게 됐을까? 그 배경에 샹송 가수 아리스티드 브뤼앙(1851~1925)이 있었다.

items.title: 알고 보면 역사가 길지 않은 각국 대표 음식들

items.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) depends on interconnected water, energy, and data systems spanning infrastructure life cycles and diverse geographies, with the potential to intensify water and energy insecurity, exacerbate social inequities and lead to cascading sustainability issues globally. items.title: Hydrogen Ion-Cut Single-Crystal Diamond Membranes for Wide and Ultrawide Bandgap Semiconductor Heterointegration
items.abstract: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. Monte Carlo simulations comparing H, He, C, and O implantation predicted a narrower vacancy-distribution profile for hydrogen under the implantation conditions examined. Raman spectroscopy was used to evaluate implantation-induced lattice damage and its recovery during annealing and membrane release, while optical bandgap analysis provided further evidence of restoration of the diamond lattice structure. After delamination and removal of residual graphitic material, freestanding SCDms with improved crystalline quality were obtained. items.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
items.abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.

items.title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. items.title: Coherent phonons in photoexcited semiconductors from first principles
items.abstract: Coherent phonons are phase-locked lattice vibrations that provide a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. Existing first-principles equation-of-motion (EOM) approaches have successfully described coherent phonons in metals and semimetals, but their extension to semiconductors requires treating the long-lived electron--hole plasma created by above-gap excitation. Here we extend the first-principles EOM framework to photoexcited semiconductors by incorporating the residual plasma force that shifts the lattice equilibrium together with the plasma-induced renormalization of the electronic structure. For monolayer MoTe$_2$, the calculated carrier-density-dependent Te displacement agrees with constrained density-functional perturbation theory only when the renormalized band structure is included. items.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
items.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
items.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange meta...

items.title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
items.abstract: Semiconductor spin qubits offer a promising route to compact and scalable quantum computers, combining long coherence times in isotopically purified silicon with compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. Beyond computational speedup, their energy efficiency is an important consideration for future large-scale systems. We evaluate the power and energy requirements of a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer by analyzing the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and benchmarking it against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). We develop a detailed energy budget, identifying cryogenic cooling as the dominant baseline contribution before quantum error correction (QEC). The comparison between the QFT and the classical FFT reveals that, for any quantum workload operating under a polynomially bounded sampling regime, the crossover in energy consumption occurs at smaller problem size...

items.title: Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
items.abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. The europium chalcogenides are natural candidates $-$ they are magnetic semiconductors whose moment of $7\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Eu$^{2+}$ ion stems from a half-filled $4f$ shell with zero orbital momentum, so that spin-orbit coupling and intrinsic damping are expected to be weak. Here we characterize an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe on diamagnetic BaF$_2$ by magnetometry and broadband ferromagnetic resonance from 10 K down to 30 mK. items.title: Novel high-pressure silicon allotrope with quartz topology from first principles
items.abstract: A novel silicon allotrope, qtz Si, with quartz topology is proposed and investigated alongside four known allotropes (dia Si-I, lon Si-IV, bsn Si-II, and gsi Si-III) using first-principles density functional theory. qtz Si is found to exhibit the smallest atom-averaged volume (18.06 A3), highest density (2.582 g/cm3), highest bulk modulus (98 GPa), and highest maximum phonon frequency (16 THz) among the five, while showing the lowest shear modulus (37 GPa). All five allotropes are confirmed to satisfy the Born stability criteria and to display positive phonon frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone, i.e., they are mechanically and dynamically stable. Electronic structure calculations show that qtz Si is a semimetal with a vanishing gap, whereas dia Si and lon Si are semiconductors, and bsn and gsi allotropes are weakly metallic. items.title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
items.abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. items.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
items.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. items.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
items.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. items.title: On-sky performance and prospects of near-infrared CMOS detectors in exoplanet detection: first year of SPIRIT
items.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs are promising targets for detecting and characterising temperate terrestrial exoplanets. Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. We find the measured precision to be consistent with our theoretical noise model, achieving sub-part-per-thousand precision under good observing conditions across targets spanning $J$-band magnitudes of 10--13. items.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. items.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
items.abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. items.abstract: We propose CktHGVAE, a heterogeneous graph variational autoencoder for transistor-level analog/mixedsignal CMOS circuits that takes not only design variables but also state variables as its inputs and outputs. items.abstract: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. items.abstract: Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. Varying the nitrogen and oxygen supply yields monoclinic beta-Ga2O3, predominantly disordered films and crystalline spinel GaON. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
items.abstract: The exploration of next-generation wide-gap semiconductors with extreme work functions is highly desirable for the continued advancement of electronic and optoelectronic devices. By using first principles calculations, we show that \b{eta}-TeO3, with a wide band gap exceeding 3 eV, emerges as a promising n-type semiconductor exhibiting ultrahigh work functions of up to ~8 eV. Intentionally or unintentionally incorporated interstitial H, Li, Na, Cu, Mg, and Zn impurities and substitutional F impurities are identified as shallow donors, whereas O vacancies act as minor carrier-compensating defects that locally trap electrons at neighbouring Te sites. The work function is evaluated across a series of low-index nonpolar surfaces. items.title: Thermal stability and structural ordering of thick Co$_2$MnAl films grown on MgO and Si substrates
items.abstract: While most studies on Co$2$MnAl (CMA) focus on the ultrathin regime for spintronic junctions, applications scaling with magnetic volume--such as Anomalous Nernst Effect (ANE) energy harvesters, integrated power inductors, and magnetic MEMS--require significantly thicker films. In this work, 750 nm thick CMA films were grown on MgO (001) and Si substrates to establish a roadmap for their thermal integration. Structural analysis reveals that B2 ordering is optimized on MgO at 600 $^\circ$C, which is important for functional devices. In contrast, samples on Si substrates exhibit a disorder transition toward the A2 phase, closely linked to diffusion-driven degradation processes. items.title: Theory of deeply subwavelength electromagnetic structuring of semiconductors due to thermal-ionization instability
items.abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. items.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. items.abstract: We present first-principles calculations of the electron-hole-pair creation energy in semiconductors and dielectrics, focusing in particular on AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2. We have employed density functional theory (DFT) to calculate the band structure, density-functional perturbation theory to obtain the phonon dispersion, and time-dependent DFT (TDDFT) to calculate the electron energy loss function (via the dielectric function). We performed full-band Monte Carlo simulations of electron thermalization for energies up to ~100 eV and calculated the average energy required to excite an electron-hole pair. We calculated pair-creation energies of approximately 12.2, 6.5, 7.3, 3.10, and 16.7 eV/pair for AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2, respectively. items.abstract: We propose a novel amorphous oxide semiconductor (AOS)-based conductive-semiconducting-conductive (CSC) MOS test structure to effectively sense, discriminate, and analyze distinct trap-induced conductance losses in AOS transistors. The CSC architecture mitigates these contact-related artifacts, enabling the decoupling of interface states and shallow states. Furthermore, the contributions from leakage, series resistance, and device-geometry effects are identified and calibrated. items.abstract: Four-level indium-gallium-zinc oxide (IGZO) 2T0C memory needs reliable state formation, sensing references, and a path from cell errors to digital weights. We analyze 107 measured DC transfer curves from 37 isolated IGZO transistors (W/L = 3/0.5 micrometers). items.title: Stateless Stochastic Computing for Generative AI on Superconducting Logic: A Model-Hardware Co-Design
items.abstract: Thermodynamic computing lets stochastic physical dynamics carry out a computation and reads out the result as a time average. Recently, thermodynamic computing has been demonstrated on several hardware platforms, including digital CMOS circuits based on stochastic computing. Superconducting single-flux-quantum (SFQ) logic offers very high clock rates and very low switching energy, but it heavily penalizes state, memory, fan-out, and feedback, i.e., exactly the per-neuron accumulators on which such designs rely. We therefore realize thermodynamic computing in SFQ logic through a co-design of a generative model and its circuit in which the datapath holds no state at all. items.abstract: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. One method of developing carbon electrodes is to 3D print polymer nanostructures on a CMOS chip, and use a thermal annealing process to pyrolyze them into carbon at high temperature, approximately 950 °C. items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. In this paper, we present TileCas, a unified, pluggable interface that enables coding agents to develop kernels across multiple editable abstraction levels. Muons must be produced, captured, cooled, accelerated, and collided before they decay. The detector must then extract clean physics from an environment dominated by decay products from the beamline. items.title: Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations
items.abstract: Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-$k$ dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs. Unlike approaches based primarily on phenomenological leakage models, our first-principles, multi-terminal quantum-tran...

items.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
items.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Unlike CPUs and GPUs, where instrumentation frameworks enable fine-grained introspection, dataflow hardware exposes little information. This lack of transparency limits the ability of compiler engineers, system designers, and application developers to analyze, tune, or debug accelerator behavior. In this paper, we introduce DFIT (DataFlow Accelerator Instrumentation Tool), an instrumentation framework designed specifically for dataflow architectures. DFIT directly instruments operations, regions, and compiler transformations at the graph IR and backend-lowering stages using semantic program representation. DFIT captures high-level, semantically meaningful data that reflect the true dataflow of computation. Thes...

items.title: Predicting Nanofabrication Variance: A Conditional Diffusion Model
items.abstract: Micro- and nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam (FIB) milling invariably deviate from input designs due to systematic and stochastic effects such as ablation-rate fluctuations, and redeposition. As such, nominally identical iterations of a given process yield a distribution of non-identical fabrication outcomes, leading to variations in the physical (optical, mechanical) properties of fabricated structures. Existing models of the milling process typically predict a single deterministic fabrication result, neglecting this variability. Here we present a conditional diffusion model that learns the statistical distribution of process outcomes conditioned on input design, enabling it to predict a realistic distribution of possible output sample structures. items.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
items.abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. items.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions in crystalline systems
items.abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moiré effects play a significant role. items.abstract: Rydberg excitons in atomically thin semiconductors offer a sensitive view of dielectric screening and electronic structure. As their spectra become increasingly well resolved, a central question is how much material information an effective Hamiltonian can predict beyond the states used to determine it. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. items.title: From Prompts to Silicon: Scaling LLM-Assisted Chip Design with the AI Hardware Design League

We present the AI Hardware Design League (AI-HDL), an international, project-based competition in which students use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively refine Verilog while simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, security review, and physical verification provide the engineering feedback needed to validate the result. Across two annual cycles, AI-HDL grew from 172 to 604 participants and from 40 to 108 teams, reaching 30 universities, six community colleges, and 19 countries. In the 2026 cohort, 68.7% of participants reported no prior Verilog experience. Twenty-two teams completed the four design phases and reached final evaluation. items.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Here, we realize a multiterminal Josephson network in a graphene Hall bar geometry with micron-scale dimensions, enabling substantial nonlocal coupling between distant terminals. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. To address this gap, we designed a laboratory activity in which students were completely involved in the experiment design, construction and operation with the final goal of measuring the speed of light with a low-cost and compact setup. items.abstract: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. Equilibrium propagation relies on a bidirectional flow of information through the physical system between input and output. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. items.abstract: Step-index few-mode fibers (FMFs) provide a compact passive platform for high-speed photonic information processing by exploiting modal dispersion to map temporal inputs into spatiotemporal representations with short-term memory. items.title: Band Tail States: Speed Bump or End of the Road for Two-Dimensional Semiconductors?
items.abstract: We propose that the path to realizing the full potential of two-dimensional (2D) electronics lies in understanding and mastering their energy band tail states (BTS). Unlike silicon, which benefits from sharp band edges (Urbach energy $E_\rm U$ ~ 10 meV), today's monolayer 2D semiconductors have rough band edges ($E_\rm U$ ~ 100 meV) caused by spatial potential inhomogeneity. Comparing a physics-based electrical model to experiments, we demonstrate that BTS cause reduced effective mobility and "slow" transistor turn-on with excessive gate voltage in monolayer 2D transistors, which sets a fundamental limit for their energy-efficient operation. We also show that BTS effects in 2D transistors could be mitigated with higher gate capacitance, with strain engineering, and by using bilayer instead of monolayer 2D channels, as long as $E_\rm U$ is reduced below ~ 50 meV. items.title: Quantum-vortex excitons beyond band topology
items.abstract: Optically exciting a typical low-dimensional semiconductor produces a nodeless \(s\)-type exciton as its lowest-energy bound state. items.title: Squeezed light from a semiconductor amplifier
items.abstract: The possibility of generating light in a squeezed quantum state during saturated light amplification in a semiconductor amplifier is theoretically analyzed. Due to four-wave mixing process during amplification, weak components of the spontaneous emission of the medium with symmetric frequency shifts relative to the strong amplified wave acquire the quantum properties of two-mode squeezed light. The squeezing of quadrature components occurs in the range of frequency shifts of several GHz ($\sim$ the inverse relaxation time of the charge carrier density) and can reach 10 dB or more under optimal conditions. The formation of a two-mode squeezing phase facilitates the observation of the squeezing effect, in which a strong wave, playing the role of a local wave, exhibits quadrature noise suppression without additional homodyne detection.

items.title: Hall conductance of dilute electrolytes from odd stochastic density functional theory
items.abstract: Electrolytes under an external magnetic field exhibit a Hall conductivity, much like metals and semiconductors. However, existing theories fail to quantitatively account for their measured Hall conductivities. To make progress toward such a theory, we develop a stochastic density functional framework for electrolytes in a magnetic field. This framework, which we dub odd SDFT, extends the celebrated stochastic density functional theory (SDFT) to incorporate transverse mobilities and chiral time-correlated noise. Using this framework, we calculate the Hall conductivity in the absence of hydrodynamic solvent effects through three approaches: (i) direct response, (ii) Green-Kubo relation, and (iii) a hybrid fluctuation-dissipation relation. We further show that odd SDFT applies more broadly to fluids with broken time-reversal and mirror symmetry, including odd-diffusive fluids and chiral act...

items.title: Vacancy aggregation enhances NV- spin coherence in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion study of multi-vacancy spin baths in semiconductors
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV-decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts t...

Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. Moreover, cross-sectional cathodoluminescence measurements on samples with high defect density demonstrate a suppressed quartet-state l...

items.title: An Emerging NVM-Based On-Chip Training Architecture with Non-Ideality Mitigation Through Bipolar Weight Distributions
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning has presented significant energy efficiency challenges to the conventional von Neumann architecture. In-memory computing (IMC) architectures based on emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) are widely regarded as a promising solution for accelerating neural network training due to their high parallelism and low power consumption. However, the intrinsic non-idealities of eNVM devices can cause conductance updates to deviate from target values, thereby limiting the performance of on-chip training. To address this challenge, this paper presents a Non-ideality Optimized eNVM Accelerator (NOVA) architecture for on-chip training. Specifically, we first fabricate a two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) and develop a conductance modulation behavioral model calibrated with experimental data. Building upon this device model, we propos...

items.title: Optically Coupled Noise Spectroscopy Quantifies Defect Passivation in Monolayer MoS2 FETs
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers are promising materials for electronic and photonic applications, yet the performance of chemical vapour deposition grown samples is severely limited by native sulphur vacancies that introduce mid-gap trap states, degrade carrier mobility, and elevate electrical noise. Here we investigate octanethiol passivation of sulphur vacancies in monolayer MoS2 field effect transistors, combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Raman scattering with electrical transport and optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy. Thiol treatment reduces the sulphur vacancy concentration from 7% to 4%, reducing the free electron density. Electrically, it increases the device resistance 35-fold while restoring gate switching with an on/off ratio of 10^4 and improving field-effect mobility from 1 to 5 cm^2/Vs. Low frequency noise spectrosc...

items.title: On-chip nanoplasma for adaptive electromagnetic protection
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor diodes have served as the primary switching elements in adaptive electromagnetic (EM) protection, yet their performance has been compromised by parasitic effects and thermal accumulation, rendering them inadequate against the rapidly evolving landscape of high-power microwave (HPM) threats. Here we show that on-chip nanoplasma switches (NPMS), composed of gallium nitride electrodes on silicon carbide substrates, exhibit superior radio frequency (RF) and thermal characteristics, positioning them as ideal field-driven switches in RF front-end protectors. By integrating NPMS into metasurfaces, antennas and circuit limiters, we achieve an adaptive response that ensures low-loss transmission for normal signals and high shielding against HPMs, while offering extended operating bandwidth and substantially higher tolerance than conventional solid-state devices...

items.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption
items.abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency on both prediction performance and energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. We numerically evaluate the performance of a chaotic time-series prediction task and estimate the energy consumption per sample using a component-level model. By optimizing the number of qu...

items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. These two modifications jointl...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Complex frequency-dependent quadrature squeezing in semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of quadrature squeezing in a quantum well laser based on a fully quantum Langevin approach. We compute the frequency-resolved squeezing map of the laser field and identify optimal squeezing curves, revealing, for the first time to our knowledge, both frequency-dependent squeezing and complex or hidden squeezing in a semiconductor laser. We further analyse the role of the linewidth enhancement factor (alpha-factor) in the emergence of these features. Our results establish semiconductor lasers as a platform for the generation of non-classical light and open new perspectives for their application in quantum communication and sensing.

items.title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
items.abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. This establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structure...

items.title: Nanoscopic Multiplexing Optical Data Storage via Chip Fabrication
items.abstract: The accelerating growth of global data demands storage technologies combining high capacity, long lifetime and low energy consumption. Optical storage is attractive for archival applications, but conventional optical writing is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution and scalability, while thermal accumulation limits high-speed writing. Here we shift optical data writing from a serial optical process to a fabrication-defined process, in which lithographic masks govern where material modification occurs. Using patterned resist masks and ion implantation, we create fluorescent information voxels with nanoscale control over millimeter-scale areas. The platform supports multilevel and multidimensional encoding by independently encoding information in fluorescence intensity and wavelength. A machine-learning-assisted super-resolution reconstruction protocol is developed to recover infor...

items.title: Absorption and Phase-Contrast Microtomography Using Direct X-Ray Detection With Commercial Off-The-Shelf CMOS Sensors
items.abstract: This work presents high-resolution X-ray microtomography based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) CMOS image sensors as direct detectors. The system uses a microfocus X-ray source in cone-beam geometry, enabling both absorption-contrast imaging, thanks to the sensor s intrinsic resolution, and phase-contrast imaging, by adjusting the object-to-sensor distance. A dynamic flat-field correction algorithm mitigates radiation-induced sensor degradation during long acquisitions. The setup provides voxel sizes from 3.9 microns to 5.2 microns, with an effective spatial resolution (FWHM) as fine as 9.6 microns in magnified phase-contrast mode (1.33x) and 21 microns in non-magnified absorption-contrast mode. Phase contrast enhances visualization of soft tissue boundaries that are difficult to visualize using absorption-contrast imaging in the same experimental configuration.

items.title: Exciton-Tunable Phase Control and Superstrong Coupling Through Multimode Polariton Engineering in Planar Waveguides
items.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical waveguides provides a versatile platform for engineering hybrid polaritonic modes and their dispersion. Here we investigate multimode exciton-photon coupling in visible semiconductor waveguides supporting several transverse electric modes. Using rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model, we show that the photonic band structure can be engineered across a range of regimes, from conventional multimode strong coupling to the superstrong coupling regime, where the Rabi splitting becomes comparable to the spacing between adjacent photonic modes. In the latter regime, hybridization between orthogonal electromagnetic modes is enabled by restricting the active material to a subregion of the mode volume where the photonic modes exhibit strong mutual overlap. This breaking of the orthogonality leads to polaritonic branches whose...

items.title: Speed Kills: Exploring Confused Deputy Attacks Through Edge AI Accelerators
items.abstract: AI Accelerators (AIAs) are specialized hardware, such as Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), that enable optimal and efficient execution of AI applications and on-device inference. The growing demand for AI applications has led to the widespread adoption of AIAs on edge and embedded devices. Unlike applications, AIAs are not bound by Operating System (OS) restrictions and have limited visibility into Application Processor (AP) security mechanisms (e.g., kernel versus application memory and process isolation). This semantic gap can lead to confused deputy vulnerabilities, where an AIA can be tricked by a malicious application into performing privileged operations on its behalf. In this paper, we conduct the first in-depth study of Confused Deputy Attacks (CDAs) using AIAs. We design DeputyHunt, a Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted framework to extract CDA-relevant information for a given AIA...

items.title: Energy Consumption in Next Generation Radio Access Networks
items.abstract: Historically, in macro-cell-based networks, the radio access network (RAN) portion accounts for the largest share of energy consumption in mobile networks. With greater densification, the transition to small cells and increased virtualization of the radio processing functions, the relative energy use of the different network segments is changing. At the same time, open radio access networks (O-RAN) have emerged as a promising approach to support this evolution through open interfaces that enable a multi-vendor environment, support for hierarchical intelligent controls, and simplified, cost-effective radio units that facilitate large-scale deployments. This paper examines the impact of these changes on energy consumption in next-generation RAN architectures through transaction-based energy models. Transaction-based network energy models were developed in 2009 to understand the evolution o...

items.title: Joint Architecture-Token-Bitwidth Multi-Axis Optimization of Vision Transformers for Semiconductor IC Packaging
items.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance in visual recognition, yet their deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments remains limited. The main challenges are their high computational cost, memory requirements, and energy consumption. While individual efficiency techniques such as neural architecture search (NAS), token compression, and low-precision inference have been extensively studied, most prior work targets only a single optimization axis, limiting overall deployment gains while preserving accuracy. In this paper, we present one of the first holistic frameworks that jointly optimizes three complementary axes: architecture, token, and bit-width. Specifically, the framework identifies compact backbones via Neural Architecture Search (AutoFormer), reduces information processing via token merging (ToMe), and accelerates per-operation execution via fp1...
